content.value_statement: Airflow DAGs often fail when retries, dependencies, and tests are designed late. This skill provides production patterns for DAG structure, sensors, alerts, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Explains core DAG design principles for idempotent, atomic, incremental, and observable workflows.
Provides TaskFlow API and PythonOperator patterns for extract, transform, load pipelines.
Shows dynamic DAG generation for similar pipelines with shared factory logic.
Covers sensors for files, upstream DAGs, and external API readiness checks.
Outlines error handling, retry behavior, alert callbacks, and cleanup paths.
Includes pytest-style DAG loading, dependency, cycle, and task logic tests.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete Airflow project scaffold.
It does not validate live scheduler, executor, or provider configuration.
Example endpoints, buckets, schedules, and owners must be replaced for each environment.
It does not handle non-Airflow orchestration tools or simple cron-only jobs.

use_cases.title: Create a New ETL DAG
use_cases.description: Design a daily or hourly pipeline with clear task boundaries, retries, ownership, and dependency flow.

use_cases.title: Standardize Airflow Patterns
use_cases.description: Define repeatable conventions for sensors, alert callbacks, dynamic DAG factories, and project structure.

use_cases.title: Review DAG Reliability
use_cases.description: Check an existing workflow for fragile dependencies, missing tests, weak retries, and unsafe backfill behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic DAG
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Apache Airflow DAG for a daily data pipeline. Include task names, dependencies, retries, schedule, and ownership notes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor to TaskFlow
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my Airflow pipeline plan into a TaskFlow API design. Explain task inputs, outputs, XCom usage, and retry settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Sensors and Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Add external dependency checks and failure alerts to this Airflow DAG design. Include sensor modes, timeouts, and callback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Airflow DAG for production readiness. Focus on idempotency, backfills, observability, testing, dynamic DAG safety, and operational runbooks.

output_examples.input: Plan a daily customer ETL workflow in Airflow.
output: A DAG outline with extract, transform, load, and notification tasks.
Recommended retry policy, start date, catchup behavior, and max active run setting.
Notes for idempotent loads, alert callbacks, and basic DAG tests.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing DAG that waits for upstream data.
output: Sensor recommendations for object storage, upstream DAG completion, and external API readiness.
Timeout and reschedule guidance to reduce worker slot usage.
A dependency plan that separates waiting, processing, cleanup, and success notification.

output_examples.input: Review a dynamic DAG factory design.
output: A checklist for stable DAG identifiers, local configuration, and predictable schedules.
Risks to avoid, including mutable task state and heavy import-time logic.
Testing guidance for DAG loading, dependency assertions, and cycle detection.

best_practices: Keep DAG files lightweight and move heavy business logic into importable modules.
Use idempotent tasks, bounded retries, clear alerts, and explicit timeouts for reliable operations.
Test DAG loading, task dependencies, cycles, and core task functions before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not use Airflow when a simple cron job or one-step shell script is enough.
Do not depend on mutable global state inside tasks or dynamic DAG factories.
Do not change production schedules, backfills, or catchup behavior without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design Apache Airflow DAGs for data pipelines, scheduled workflows, sensors, alerts, and tests.

faq.question: Does it create a complete Airflow repository?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, and review guidance that you adapt to your own repository.

faq.question: Can it help with TaskFlow API designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TaskFlow patterns for task definitions, XCom passing, and ETL task flow.

faq.question: Does it cover external dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers file sensors, upstream DAG sensors, and external API readiness checks.

faq.question: Can it review existing DAGs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide reviews for dependencies, retries, observability, testing, and backfill safety.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Apache Airflow?
faq.answer: Only partly. The guidance is specific to Airflow and is not meant for other orchestrators.
